A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same nGPT research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-versus-nGPT training experiments, downstream task evaluations, PG19 length extrapolation, parameter analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds translation results, a length-extrapolation control and further ablation and timing results.

M1.justification: Section 2.6 adds optional matrix normalization during the forward pass alongside normalization after training steps. This is a limited procedural option; the default architecture, objectives and update equations remain unchanged. SLERP and LERP were already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 10 adds WMT14-FR-EN, testing French-to-English translation given five example pairs. This extends coverage to a distinct cross-lingual task while retaining OpenWebText training, the five original downstream tasks and PG19.

E2.justification: v2 adds nGPT without QK normalization to the PG19 comparison and a SLERP variant to Table 6. These are focused additions to the comparator sets in those experiments. ReZero and NormFormer receive discussion but are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce five-example translation measured with BLEU and a PG19 comparison using 0.5B models trained with 1k context. Table 6 also adds training time per step as a comparison metric. The established training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 14-right tests whether QK normalization contributes to length extrapolation, extending the earlier in-distribution removal ablation. Table 6 adds a direct LERP-versus-SLERP accuracy, loss and timing comparison. Existing scaling-factor ablations and parameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained parameter-distribution histograms do not constitute run-to-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds WMT14 BLEU curves and PG19 results showing poorer extrapolation without QK normalization. Table 6 newly reports step times of 0.657, 0.576 and 0.726 seconds for baseline, QK-normalization removal and SLERP, respectively; SLERP achieves 54.80% average accuracy and a -0.08% relative validation-loss change. Original aggregate ablation results remain, but individual task scores are removed from Table 6.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an algebraic comparison of residual scaling: ReZero permits compensating changes to its scalar and output matrices, whereas nGPT's normalized block output supports a different scaling-invariance interpretation. NormFormer update equations are also examined. The existing SLERP/LERP mathematics and Riemannian derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: hyperspherical normalization, interpretation as a variable-metric optimizer and a reported 4–20-fold reduction in required training steps. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the earlier recommendation that QK normalization can be removed with little performance impact: similar in-distribution performance conceals worse length extrapolation. Appendix A.8 discusses normalization and low-rank attention as explanations. Section 3.2 also makes the proposed connection between MLP capacity and larger eigen learning rates explicitly conditional.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 newly discloses bfloat16 matrix storage, the internal Megatron-LM-based implementation and access to a public nanoGPT reimplementation. It cautions that the public implementation reproduces results only qualitatively and explains that optimizer-held parameters must also be normalized. These are disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 substantially expand research positioning through detailed comparisons with ReZero and NormFormer, discussion of Weight Norm Control as a precursor, and connections to diffusion-model normalization, hyperspherical optimization and Hopfield memory. Additional citations also contextualize logit scaling and low-rank attention.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. v2 adds supplementary introductory notes, expands selected appendix explanations, revises a few interpretive paragraphs and updates the publication header and cross-references. This is localized expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel translation figure, redraws the PG19 figure with logarithmic axes and an additional comparison panel, and restructures Table 6 around timing and aggregate performance. Other figures and tables are largely retained, with appendix relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional validation and corrects practical guidance about removing QK normalization by documenting its extrapolation cost. Timing measurements, clearer positioning against related architectures and implementation disclosures improve assessment and usability. These focused gains outweigh the loss of individual task scores in Table 6, although the public code is explicitly only a qualitative reproduction and the central method and evidence remain largely unchanged.
